Hi Gina — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise Q&A you can forward to your privacy team; I flagged two items for Karthik (retention enforcement and legal hold behavior).

Q: What retention windows can customers choose for tenant audit & access logs?
A: Customers can pick one of three supported retention policy buckets at tenant creation or via the Console API: 30 days (short), 365 days (standard), or 7 years (long-term archiving). We also support a custom SLA-backed retention (e.g., multiyear) via Dedicated/Private contracts — requires an agreement.

Q: Are exports region-locked?
A: Yes — exports honor the tenant's data residency setting. Exports generated from a US-resident tenant are produced and stored in US regions only. For Private deployments, exports remain within the customer VPC/region.

Q: What export formats and delivery methods are available?
A: Supported formats: compressed JSONL (default), Parquet (columnar), CSV (schema-limited) and encrypted tar.gz bundles. Delivery options: signed HTTPS URLs (S3-compatible presigned link), direct push to a customer S3/GCS bucket (with customer-provided credentials), and one-time secure FTP (enterprise). We can also provide incremental snapshot exports that include change deltas for a configurable window.

Q: How is exported data encrypted?
A: Bundles are encrypted at rest with customer-managed KMS keys (KMIP/HSM available for Private) or Redwood-managed KMS. All in-transit transfers use TLS 1.2+. You can request envelope encryption if you need extra separation.

Q: What triggers deletion of audit/access logs?
A: Deletion happens based on the configured retention policy (time-based expiration). There are three primary deletion paths:
  - automated expiration: system sweep removes records once they exceed retention window;
  - tenant-initiated purge: tenant admin can schedule a manual purge (subject to legal hold checks);
  - admin reclaim: constrained situations where operations performs a hard-delete under an approved support ticket (rare, audited).

Q: How do legal holds / preservation locks work?
A: A legal hold will suspend automated expiration and tenant-initiated purges for the affected tenant or specific resource keys for the duration of the hold. Legal-hold status is reflected in the Console and via API. Removing a legal hold requires the same principal who placed it or an authorized compliance approver and is recorded in an immutable audit trail.

Notes: 1) For compliance audits we can produce a manifest (index) file alongside exports to help with verification. 2) Export SLA: goal is 48–72 hours for large bulk exports (>1TB), typical small exports are same/next business day.

I'll let Karthik add any implementation caveats.

— Hannah

> A: Deletion happens based on the configured retention policy (time-based expiration).

Hi Gina — some implementation details to call out from Ops/Platform side: 

1) Deletion enforcement: the sweeper runs in two phases: a metadata pass (fast) and the blob remove pass (durable delete). For long-retention tenants we convert older data to immutable cold-storage segments before final erase; this reduces operational cost but still adheres to the retention window.

2) Preservation granularity: holds can be applied at tenant-level, application-id level, or specific resource ID (e.g., session/trace id). When a hold is active we keep both metadata and payload until released.

3) Auditability: every export and delete operation is logged to an immutable export-events log (we sign the manifest). We can provide a signed checksum/manifest that you can validate during ingestion.

4) Edge-case: if your compliance team requires immediate emergency preservation across multiple tenants, we can flip a read-only snapshot and provide a forensics export; this action is irreversible until the hold is released and requires a signed request.

If you want, we can include an example retention policy JSON and a sample manifest.
